title: "Federated Learning"
description: "A training approach where participants collaboratively learn a model while keeping raw data local."
term: "Federated Learning"
letter: "F"

## Simple explanation

Federated learning trains a shared model using data held by multiple
participants without requiring them to send all raw records to one
central location.

## Technical explanation

In a common cross-device setup, a server distributes model parameters,
clients train locally, and the server aggregates updates. Variants
include cross-silo training among organizations. Federated learning
reduces central collection of raw data but does not by itself provide
formal privacy guarantees.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Federated approaches can support learning across devices or institutions
with data-locality constraints. They face challenges including
non-identical data distributions, unreliable clients, communication cost,
poisoning risks, and privacy leakage through updates.

## How it works

The coordinator selects participants and sends a model. Each participant
computes local updates on its own data and returns an update or related
summary. The coordinator aggregates updates and repeats the process.
Secure aggregation and differential privacy may add protections.

## Practical example

Several hospitals can collaboratively train a model by computing updates
locally and sharing protected model updates rather than pooling patient
records in one central dataset.

## Common misconceptions

- Keeping raw data local does not guarantee that model updates reveal
  nothing about that data.
- Federated learning is not the same as decentralized inference.
- Privacy, fairness, and security require additional design and analysis.
